discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 201057 CCA
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
557 AM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Very mild with highs in the mid 60s through Saturday.

- Scattered showers along a cold front Sunday afternoon (80%
  chance).

- Seasonable next week with highs near 40 with the forecast 
  leaning dry up through Thanksgiving.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 152 AM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

High pressure over the central Appalachians promotes southerly 
surface flow on its western edge. Combined with unseasonable upper-
level ridging (579dm!) and our mild stretch of weather continues with 
highs in the mid-60s both today and Saturday. Through November 18, 
the average temperature this month of about 47.5 degrees ranks as 
the 17-18th warmest (South Bend, Fort Wayne respectively) on record. 
This warmth fades away with a cold front arriving Sunday. High 
pressure moves offshore in response a trough emerging over the 
Central Plains. A parent low tracks northeast across the Hudson Bay 
with an elongated cold front in its wake. Moisture return into the 
front is acceptable, with a hint of Gulf moisture slipping poleward 
along a subtropical ridge. This results in high-confidence POPs 
(around 80%). Yet, forward motion is swift and upper-level forcing 
is displaced across central WI resulting in small rain amounts 
(0.10" or less). Hardly a washout Sunday with rain arriving from 
west to east starting in the early afternoon. With this afternoon 
timing, northwest Ohio faces a pleasant Sunday with plenty of dry 
time and highs in the 60s, while northwest Indiana will see falling 
temperatures in the late afternoon. 

Highs in the 40s for the remainder of the 7-day forecast period will 
be rude awakening but close to normal for the final full week of 
November. Before Canadian high pressure settles over the Midwest, a 
modest upper-level impulse ripples through the northwest flow 
perhaps sparking a brief period of the Lake Effect early Tuesday 
morning. The magnitude of the cold air (-8C at 850mb) is 
appropriate, yet high pressure may quickly undercut any growing 
equilibrum-levels disrupting any emerging lake effect.

Late-week remains seasonably cool with the prospects of a low 
developing over the far eastern US. The magnitude of any trough 
remains in flux as noted by 500-mb height run-to-run deltas. 
Preexisting high pressure may steer any precipitation elsewhere but 
in absence of any true model consistency, we'll offer 20-30% POPs 
Wednesday night through Thursday for the time being.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 557 AM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

The high pressure center translates eastward and a warm advection 
pattern continues to encroach on the area. Forcing is still far 
enough away that the area will continue to remain dry through the 
period. As such, expect VFR conditions to continue. Winds will 
just get to 10 kts sustained at SBN as the combination of a low 
level jet and adequate mixing just gets to SBN during the late 
afternoon. Initially southwest winds back southerly by 
period's-end.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Brown
AVIATION...Roller

spc.text:
SPC AC 200542

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1142 PM CST Thu Nov 19 2026

   Valid 201200Z - 211200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not forecast across the U.S. today and tonight.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At mid-levels, a shortwave ridge will move into the Great Lakes
   region today as a large-scale trough moves through the Intermountain
   West. Ahead of the trough, southwesterly mid-level flow will become
   established over the central U.S. In response, a broad low-level jet
   will strengthen from the Great Plains into the Upper Mississippi
   Valley. Strong lift associated with the low-level jet and elevated
   instability will contribute to a potential for isolated
   thunderstorms tonight from central Nebraska into southwest
   Minnesota. Additional storms will be possible within a moist airmass
   over the Florida Peninsula. No severe threat is forecast across the
   continental U.S. today and tonight.

   ..Broyles.. 11/20/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 200658

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1258 AM CST Fri Nov 20 2026

   Valid 211200Z - 221200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PORTIONS OF
   NORTH TEXAS...WESTERN OKLAHOMA INTO CENTRAL KANSAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe storms are possible over the central and
   southern Plains Saturday.

   ...Central and Southern Plains..
   An upper trough over the Rockies will move eastward as the primary
   shortwave moves out of the Four Corners into the Plains by early
   Sunday. Strong ascent will overspread portions of KS/OK/TX beginning
   Saturday afternoon as a weak lee cyclone over southeast CO will move
   eastward with a cold front and surface trough. The low will aid
   modest moisture return with low to mid 50s F surface dewpoints
   likely as far north as central KS. Steepening mid-level lapse rates
   of 7-7.5 C/km atop the moistening boundary layer should allow for
   gradual destabilization through the day. While not overly large,
   MUCAPE of around 500 J/kg should be sufficient for thunderstorm
   development, Saturday afternoon continuing into the evening and
   overnight hours. Strengthening deep-layer wind fields would favor
   some potential for organized linear clusters along the front, with
   more cellular potential farther southwest.

   Model guidance has trended slower with the upper trough which will
   likely limit the amount destabilization across these area. Low-level
   moisture will be somewhat marginal and surface temperatures
   relatively cool (particularly into Kansas). Still, isolated severe
   potential remains evident with the strongest storms. Isolated hail
   and some damaging gust potential may continue into the overnight
   hours as the front surges eastward.

   ...Coastal Carolinas...
   A coastal low in the western Atlantic is forecast to deepen quickly
   along the Gulf stream as it moves northeastward Saturday and
   Saturday night. A fairly strong coastal front is expected to be in
   place with cool dry northwesterly low-level flow ongoing inland.
   Some model guidance shows the surface low tracking onshore allowing
   for some moisture advection inland late. Should this occur, strong
   low-level wind fields and a very moist environment could allow for a
   couple of shallow rotating storms across parts of the coastal
   Carolinas. Sporadic damaging gusts or a brief tornado are possible.
   However, very weak buoyancy will be in place and significant track
   uncertainty exists. Thus, confidence in severe weather probabilities
   is very low.

   ..Lyons.. 11/20/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 200829

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0229 AM CST Fri Nov 20 2026

   Valid 221200Z - 231200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered thunderstorms are possible over parts of the middle and
   lower Mississippi valley Sunday.

   ...Mid to Lower MS Valley...
   The upper trough and associated cold front over the southern Plains
   will move eastward into the middle and lower MS Valley and slowly
   weaken through Sunday. Continued southerly low-level flow will
   transport low 60s F surface dewpoints as far north as AR allowing
   for modest destabilization. Remnant thunderstorms are likely to be
   ongoing ahead of the cold front from the Midwest, south toward the
   Ozarks and Sabine River early Sunday morning. These may reinvigorate
   somewhat as they move into the gradually destabilizing air mass
   across AR and LA.

   Low 60s F surface dewpoints should allow for around 500 J/kg of
   MLCAPE from northern LA into southern AR, though lapse rates are
   expected to remain modest. Mid-level winds are also forecast to
   weaken somewhat through the day as the shortwave trough moves
   northeastward. Still, 20-30kt of deep-layer shear could support a
   few stronger clusters or transient supercells through Sunday
   afternoon, but confidence is not high. If a few stronger storms do
   form, isolated hail and damaging gusts would be possible, most
   likely across southern AR, northern LA and perhaps far western MS.
   Any convection should weaken overnight as the front moves eastward
   into a cooler and drier air mass. Given the uncertainty, severe
   probabilities will be withheld for now.

   ...Eastern Carolinas...
   While the exact track of the circulation of the coastal low remains
   unclear, model confidence remains high that it will begin to move
   northeastward away from the coast through Sunday. A few
   thunderstorms are possible early in the day before the coastal front
   moves offshore and cooler/drier conditions return. Given the weak
   buoyancy, severe storms are unlikely.

   ..Lyons.. 11/20/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
